execution: Run these scenarios in disposable sample repositories with local synthetic data. Create the fixtures described by each setup; fixtures and an automated agent runner are not bundled. Inspect actual artifacts and record which scenarios were exercised. Do not treat this scenario list as passing test results.

evals.name: browser-and-cli-without-specifications
evals.setup: A small local web application with a persisted create/list workflow and an independently runnable CLI that lists the same records. Include startup commands and tests, but no docs/specs or docs/detailed-designs. Include a shared library and test runner.
evals.prompt: Create a demo video for every application in this repository.
expected: Discovers the web app and CLI; excludes the library and test runner.
Infers workflows without requiring new specifications or designs.

Produces two playable WebM files with an Opus narration track synthesized by edge-tts using en-US-AndrewMultilingualNeural, captions matching the narration text, and posters from decoded successful footage, with measured metadata and accurate chapters.
CLI output comes from commands executed during capture; assertions verify persisted records.
Documents and successfully exercises a clean rerun command.

evals.name: multiple-apps-and-shared-data
evals.setup: A monorepo with admin and public web applications served by one host, an independently executable API, and a worker. Admin publishes a record, the public app reads it, and the worker processes a job. Include a third-party database service and stale specifications claiming an unimplemented feature.
evals.prompt: Record each application so a viewer understands the whole platform.
expected: Accounts for four first-party applications and excludes the database from the video count.
Orders stories by data dependencies, keeps fixtures consistent, and documents full-sequence and individual rerun prerequisites.
Shows real API interactions and correlates a worker result with the submitted job.
Documents the unimplemented feature without simulating it or describing it as working.

evals.name: partial-startup-and-resource-ownership
evals.setup: An existing unrelated listener and a development database contain sentinel data. The proposed demo port is occupied. Arrange for a required service to fail readiness after another owned service starts. Include an independent working CLI.
evals.prompt: Create demos for all apps; keep going if one is blocked.
expected: Chooses isolated ports/storage or reports a precise blocker; preserves sentinel data and the unrelated listener.
Bounds startup and cleans up the owned service despite partial setup failure.
Completes the CLI recording and reports partial completion with actionable startup diagnostics.

evals.name: failed-replacement-and-product-bug
evals.setup: Existing successful video, poster, and chapter documentation have known hashes. A product image endpoint now returns 404 while the UI still sets the expected src and alt attributes. A second application works.
expected: Detects that the image did not load, fails the affected take, and does not weaken assertions or fix product code by default.
Preserves the previous affected artifact set and labels it as retained from an earlier run.
Publishes the independent successful recording and identifies the broken workflow as blocked.
A simulated promotion failure restores the prior complete artifact set rather than mixing versions.

evals.name: native-and-interactive-capture-unavailable
evals.setup: A native app and interactive terminal UI have runnable entrypoints, but the execution environment lacks desktop capture and PTY support. Include a noninteractive CLI that can run and be captured.
evals.prompt: Make a video of every executable application.
expected: Identifies missing capture capabilities early and names both blockers.
Does not replace the native app with a mock UI or the TUI with a pipes-only transcript.
Captures the noninteractive CLI with actual execution and a disclosed presentation method.
Does not claim complete coverage.

evals.name: scope-and-empty-repository
evals.setup: First use a library-only repository with build scripts and tests. Then use a multi-app repository with a user request explicitly limited to its marketing application.
evals.prompt: Create demo videos for this repository, respecting the applications I selected.
expected: Explains that the library-only repository has no executable product to record.
For the scoped request, records only the selected application and labels other applications as out of the user's scope.
Preserves unrelated existing demo content.

evals.name: narration-tools-unavailable
evals.setup: The browser application from scenario 1 in an environment where the edge-tts package cannot be installed or synthesis has no network access, while Playwright, Chromium, and ffmpeg are available.
evals.prompt: Create a demo video for the web application in this repository.
expected: Detects the missing narration capability before or during synthesis and names the exact installation or connectivity step that remains.
Keeps the recording and its narration text in staging; does not promote a silent WebM into docs/demo/ or describe it as complete.
Does not substitute silence, placeholder audio, or a transcript for the narration.
Reports partial completion with the rerun commands that will produce the narrated video once the tool is available.
